messages:
alex: Heads-up: automated kernel image rollout to GPU nodegroup in us-west-2 is causing nodes to cordon/drain repeatedly and some pods are CrashLooping. Symptoms look CNI-related. Anyone from infra around to help triage?

mira: I'm oncall, ping me which nodegroup/AMI the pipeline pushed to?

ops-oncall: infra-bot deployed image update: aws-gpu-ami-20260308 -> kernel 5.19.12 to autoscaling-group/gpu-workers-usw2 at 2026-03-10T03:40Z :robot_face:

samir: can you paste kubelet / aws-vpc-cni logs? my hunch is the kernel change removed host modules the CNI expects.

mira: grabbing logs now, tailing aws-node on a flapping node:

```
kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/aws-node -l k8s-app=aws-node --tail 200
E0309 03:42:12.123456 1 main.go:200] failed to configure ENI: failed to load iptables modules: modprobe: FATAL: Module br_netfilter not found in directory /lib/modules/5.19.12
E0309 03:42:12.123789 1 main.go:210] reconciliation failed, retrying
```

mira: also seeing kube-proxy warn that bridge-nf-call-iptables is unset so iptables rules are effectively ignored.

alex: confirms the AMI change removed br_netfilter. Terraform plan shows launch_template.user_data updated and image-updater pushed ami-20260308. Looks like the image-builder omitted packaging the netfilter module.

samir: short mitigation options: 1) rollback ASG to previous AMI, 2) patch launch template user-data to modprobe br_netfilter at boot + persist sysctl, or 3) bump CNI to a fallback image that tolerates missing module during bootstrap (less ideal).

mira: attempting quick patch: helm upgrade aws-vpc-cni --namespace kube-system --set image.tag=1.12.0-fallback --reuse-values

infra-bot: deploy-bot started helm upgrade aws-vpc-cni on cluster: staging-usw2

mira: helm is failing because daemonset can't start on nodes that lack the kernel module. So helm won't finish until node AMI is fixed.

samir: I'll run a tainted one-node repro to validate the AMI in our dev account before we roll further. Meanwhile we should rollback.

alex: found terraform drift: module.node_groups.aws_launch_template.gpu[0] image_id: "ami-20260112" => "ami-20260308". That was auto-applied by the image-updater pipeline at 03:40Z. Need a gate for gpu nodegroups.

mira: propose immediate plan: (a) rollback ASG to ami-20260112 (fast path), (b) pause image-updater and add kernel-module validation step, (c) add systemd unit in user_data to modprobe br_netfilter and set sysctl net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1 as a durable guard.

ops-oncall: starting rollback now. terraform apply -target=module.node_groups.aws_launch_template.gpu[0] in progress.

mira: first rolled node now shows aws-node healthy, CNI errors cleared for that instance. Replacements are progressing.

samir: follow-ups to capture in playbook: ["add preflight check in image-updater: verify lsmod br_netfilter and sysctl bridge-nf-call-iptables","add user_data systemd unit to modprobe br_netfilter and persist sysctl","require manual approval for image changes to gpu nodegroups via terraform plan alert"]

alex: +1. Please open a short RFC to gate automatic AMI updates for infra-critical nodegroups.

mira: created RFC draft: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/infra-image-gate-2026 (owners: @samir @alex @ops-oncall).

ops-oncall: marking incident resolved — cluster health normalized, pod restarts returned to baseline :white_check_mark:.

mira: I'll follow up with a helm chart bump for aws-vpc-cni to improve graceful retry semantics and we'll add AMI validation to our CI image pipeline.

alex: filing postmortem with timeline, terraform diff, and rollout logs.

samir: added quick rollback snippet to playbook:```terraform apply -target=module.node_groups.aws_launch_template.gpu[0]```

mira: closing thread. keep an eye on us-west-2 autoscaler metrics for 24h :eyes:
